IPC_302.title: Punishment for murder
IPC_302.text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

IPC_304.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
IPC_304.text: Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder shall be punished with imprisonment for life or up to ten years and fine.

IPC_304B.title: Dowry death
IPC_304B.text: Death of a woman by burns or bodily injury within seven years of marriage, connected with dowry cruelty, is a dowry death.

IPC_354.title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
IPC_354.text: Assaulting or using criminal force on a woman intending to outrage her modesty is punishable with 1-5 years imprisonment and fine.

IPC_376.title: Punishment for rape
IPC_376.text: Rape is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of not less than ten years, extendable to life imprisonment, and fine.

IPC_379.title: Punishment for theft
IPC_379.text: Theft is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.

IPC_420.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
IPC_420.text: Cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.

IPC_498A.title: Husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty
IPC_498A.text: Subjecting a married woman to cruelty by husband or his relatives is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

IPC_506.title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
IPC_506.text: Criminal intimidation is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or seven years for threats of death/grievous hurt, or fine, or both.

CrPC_41.title: When police may arrest without warrant
CrPC_41.text: Police may arrest without a warrant for cognizable offences committed in their presence or on reasonable suspicion.

CrPC_154.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
CrPC_154.text: Oral or written information about a cognizable offence must be reduced to writing by the police (an FIR), with a free copy given to the informant.

CrPC_161.title: Examination of witnesses by police
CrPC_161.text: Police may examine any person acquainted with the facts of a case during investigation; the person must answer truthfully except self-incriminating questions.

CrPC_167.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours
CrPC_167.text: If investigation is not complete within 24 hours, the accused must be produced before a magistrate, who may authorize detention up to 15 days at a time, subject to 60/90-day outer limits and default bail thereafter.

CrPC_173.title: Report of police officer on completion of investigation (chargesheet)
CrPC_173.text: On completing investigation, police must file a report (chargesheet) with the magistrate stating whether an offence appears to have been committed.

CrPC_197.title: Prosecution of judges and public servants
CrPC_197.text: Prosecuting a public servant for acts done in official duty requires prior government sanction.

Constitution_Art14.title: Right to Equality
Constitution_Art14.text: The State shall not deny equality before the law or equal protection of laws to any person.

Constitution_Art19.title: Freedom of speech and expression, etc.
Constitution_Art19.text: Citizens have the right to free speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession, subject to reasonable restrictions.

Constitution_Art21.title: Protection of life and personal liberty
Constitution_Art21.text: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law; interpreted to include dignity, privacy, and a speedy trial.

Constitution_Art22.title: Protection against arrest and detention
Constitution_Art22.text: Arrested persons must be informed of the grounds of arrest, allowed legal counsel, and produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

Constitution_Art32.title: Right to Constitutional Remedies
Constitution_Art32.text: Citizens may move the Supreme Court directly to enforce fundamental rights via writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, and certiorari.

Constitution_Art226.title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
Constitution_Art226.text: High Courts may issue writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for enforcement of rights.

BNS_103.title: Punishment for murder by five or more persons on grounds of race, caste, etc.
BNS_103.text: A group of five or more acting in concert to commit murder on grounds such as race, caste, or community is punishable with death or life imprisonment and fine.

BNS_109.title: Attempt to murder
BNS_109.text: An act done with the intention or knowledge that would amount to murder if death resulted is punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.

RTI_6.title: Request for obtaining information
RTI_6.text: Any person may request information in writing or electronically, in English, Hindi, or the local official language, without giving reasons.

RTI_7.title: Disposal of request
RTI_7.text: Information must be provided within 30 days of a request, or within 48 hours if it concerns life or liberty.

CPA_35.title: Manner of filing complaint before District Commission
CPA_35.text: Consumers, associations, or government bodies may file a complaint about goods or services before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

CPA_38.title: Procedure on admission of complaint
CPA_38.text: After admitting a complaint, the District Commission notifies the opposite party, who must respond within 30-45 days, before deciding on merits.
